findings.title: The version bump to 3 creates a version-number collision with the cited product law, and this role field keeps two bare 'v3' tokens, making its operative clause read as self-referential.
findings.detail: The field reads: 'Recorded provider-only-output-contract.v3. NT-4 and NT-7 input and pass words are quoted. Product law stays on v3. g20-fixture-corpus.v3 does not replace v3 and does not SATISFY DR-133.' The final clause places the subject's own fully-qualified name and a bare version token denoting a different artifact inside one sentence. Read literally, 'g20-fixture-corpus.v3 does not replace v3' asserts that the artifact does not replace itself, which is vacuous and inverts the field's actual purpose, namely to record that the fixture corpus does not displace provider-only-output-contract.v3 as product law. These are the only two bare 'v3' tokens in the artifact; every other version token in every other field is noun-qualified or fully dotted, which I established by sweeping all string leaves.
findings.whyThisIsNewAtV3: This is not inherited text that a previous review passed over. At g20-fixture-corpus.v2 the same sentence read 'g20-fixture-corpus.v2 does not replace v3', where the only artifact at version 3 in scope was the product law and the bare token was unambiguous. The collision is created by this successor's own version bump, and the field was retargeted for the speaker without being re-examined for the collision the retargeting introduced.
findings.whyItMatters: It is the same defect family and the same field class — a current-standing basedOn.*.role clause that does not name its referent unambiguously — as the unlabeled Codex SHOULD-FIX that this successor exists to land. These role fields are consumed per entry as the candidate's standing explanation of its relationship to one cited input, so a reader of basedOn.d136.role alone gets a clause whose literal reading is empty. The artifact also establishes the remedy itself and then applies it in the wrong places: five basedOn entries end with the disambiguator "Not this artifact's version number." — leftoverJoinV6, sdkJoinV6, g21FixtureCorpusV1, predecessorV1 and predecessorV2 — none of which numerically collides with version 3, while the two entries that do cite a version-3 artifact, d136 and productLaw, carry no guard, and d136 additionally carries the bare tokens. The anti-collision discipline is applied where it is not needed and omitted where it is.
findings.whyNotMustFix: No byte claim is false. The D-136 pin is correct, provider-only-output-contract.v3 is verified at ef2a7416…, the NT input and pass words really are quoted from it, DR-133 is not SATISFIED anywhere, and binds remains NOTHING. A careful reader recovers the intended referent from the preceding sentence 'Product law stays on v3.' This is a successor-attribution and wording defect, not a semantic takeover, which is the same grade Codex assigned to the structurally analogous defect at v2.
findings.repairShape: In basedOn.d136.role, replace both bare tokens with the fully-qualified name: 'Recorded provider-only-output-contract.v3. NT-4 and NT-7 input and pass words are quoted. Product law stays on provider-only-output-contract.v3. g20-fixture-corpus.v3 does not replace provider-only-output-contract.v3 and does not SATISFY DR-133.' Optionally extend the artifact's own convention by appending "Not this artifact's version number." to basedOn.d136.role and basedOn.productLaw.role, which are the two entries that now numerically collide with the subject's version. Change nothing else: the pin, the fixtures, the derivation rule and every other field are correct and should carry forward byte-identically.
